title: A baseline-risk bridge across a disconnected network
question: When disconnected subnetworks are linked through exchangeable baseline risks, does study-level design nuisance pass into the cross-gap contrast, and can design covariates separate it from prognosis?
design: Two subnetworks with prognostic drift, a design nuisance on the baseline and a design covariate overlapping the gap or not; exchangeable-baseline bridge with and without design adjustment. 24 cells, 2000 replicates each.
answer: A baseline-risk bridge transports whatever makes the subnetworks' baselines differ. When a design nuisance (such as an endpoint definition) coincided with the subnetwork it passed one for one into the cross-gap contrast (bias 0.2 to 0.7) and no adjustment was possible. When a quarter of trials used the other definition, adjusting for it removed the nuisance but not prognostic drift between subnetworks (bias 0.19 to 0.20).
findings: Refuting sentence fails: without crossover, adjustment possible in 0% of analyses and bridge bias 0.207 to 0.712.
With 25% crossover and no drift, adjusted bias within 0.003.
With prognostic drift 0.2, adjusted bias 0.191 to 0.204.
not_answered: Study-level summaries, no Bayesian arm-based model or commensurate prior, one design covariate. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Cross-gap contrast C versus A on the log odds scale
methods_compared: bridge adjusted for a design covariate
